oe_leaders_trust:
A new senior-level team member should be properly briefed on the existing organizational structure, workflow, and the team’s past achievements and performance.

Having a clear understanding of the existing processes and vendor/customer relationships will help ensure a smooth transition and maintain a healthy relationship with both vendors and customers.

It is important to avoid unnecessary disruption to the existing line of work, as frequent changes in established processes can create a negative impact on the vendor side, which may ultimately affect service delivery and customer satisfaction.

Therefore, any changes to the existing workflow should be implemented after understanding the background, current responsibilities, past performance, and business relationships, with a focus on maintaining continuity while making improvements where required.
oe_feel_valued:
If there is an issue, it should be evaluated objectively by keeping the interests and perspectives of both entities on the same platform.

It is important to understand the complete facts and assess the situation based on its actual business impact rather than giving unnecessary importance to an issue that may not require such escalation.

As a natural human tendency, there can sometimes be a tendency to overemphasize certain matters. Therefore, decisions should be based on facts, the actual impact on business, and the interests of both parties, rather than on assumptions or individual perceptions.

This balanced approach will help maintain healthy vendor and customer relationships while ensuring that genuine issues receive the appropriate attention.
oe_fairness_concern:
The biggest concern regarding fairness is the consistency in how decisions, responsibilities, and performance are evaluated across individuals and teams.

At times, existing processes and contributions may not be fully considered before making changes or assigning responsibilities. A new senior-level member should have sufficient understanding of the existing structure, past achievements, performance, and established vendor/customer relationships before making significant changes.

Similarly, when an issue arises, it should be assessed objectively by considering the perspectives and interests of all parties involved. Avoiding unnecessary escalation or giving disproportionate importance to minor issues would help create a more balanced and fair working environment.

Greater transparency, consistency, and fact-based decision-making would strengthen employees' confidence that decisions are being made fairly.

I would never want us to lose the culture of collaboration, responsiveness, and ownership that helps us deliver results and maintain long-term business relationships. This would reduce misunderstandings, avoid duplication of work, and help teams support each other more effectively. It would also help us maintain healthy and professional relationships with our vendors, whose support and cooperation are essential to serving our customers effectively.

At the same time, feedback should always be given with professionalism and respect. No employee, regardless of their level or position, should be humiliated or spoken to in a manner that compromises their dignity or creates an uncomfortable working environment. A healthy workplace should allow people at every level to express their views respectfully, receive constructive feedback, and be held accountable based on the same standards. This would create greater trust, fairness, and mutual respect within the team.

If any new recruitment takes place within the organisation, particularly at a senior level, the senior leadership should take the responsibility of guiding the new members about the existing workflow, processes, responsibilities, and working structure of the organisation.

This will help new recruits understand how the organisation is currently functioning and give them clarity about their own roles and responsibilities. It will also help prevent confusion or unnecessary overlap with the responsibilities and work already being handled by existing team members.

This kind of guidance will also build trust among existing employees. They will feel assured that the work and responsibilities they are handling are known and recognised by senior leadership, and that their contribution and areas of responsibility are being properly observed and supported.

Secondly, whenever a suggestion, concern, or issue arises within the existing workflow, senior leaders should give it proper consideration and make an effort to find a suitable solution.

If the same concern or issue is being raised by multiple employees or by different departments, it should be given particular attention. Such recurring feedback may indicate that there is an underlying issue in the existing process or workflow that needs to be reviewed.

Listening to such feedback and taking appropriate corrective action will help improve the overall working process, reduce confusion, and make employees feel that their concerns are being heard and valued.

oe_fairness_concern:
Maintaining a certain level of transparency and giving appropriate consideration to an issue when similar concerns are raised independently by more than one employee against a particular situation, individual, or department is important for ensuring a fair and balanced judgement.

When multiple employees raise concerns about the same issue or behaviour, it should be carefully considered rather than being viewed as an isolated matter. Addressing such concerns appropriately also helps other employees understand that certain behaviours or situations will not be acceptable at any level of the organisation.

A transparent and consistent approach can create greater trust between employees and the organisation. It provides clarity that the same rules, standards, and expectations apply equally to everyone, regardless of their position, role, or department.

This can ultimately strengthen the bond between employees and the organisation by promoting fairness, accountability, mutual respect, and confidence that concerns will be handled objectively and consistently.

oe_one_change:
Recruitment should be based on the experience, skills, and requirements of the particular role. Wherever freshers are recruited, they should first be given proper training and an understanding of the basic business processes before being assigned major responsibilities.

Freshers should be given a supportive and friendly environment where they can learn, ask questions, and understand the organisation’s way of working without hesitation. As part of their initial training, it would also be beneficial to give them exposure to different departments so that they can understand the overall business, how different teams coordinate with each other, and how their own role fits into the larger workflow.

Maintaining a Professional and Disciplined Work Environment
Existing senior employees and team leaders should address concerns or disciplinary matters with employees in a professional and respectful manner. Wherever there is a need to discuss an employee’s performance, conduct, or any other concern, it would be better to call the concerned employee to a cabin or private meeting and discuss the matter in a disciplined and constructive tone.

Corrective feedback is important, but addressing employees by yelling or reprimanding them openly on the work floor can create a negative impression and may affect the overall work environment and employee morale. Private and respectful communication can help resolve such matters more effectively while maintaining the dignity of everyone involved.

Communication Outside Office Hours
For calls or queries that arise after office hours, on holidays, or when a particular employee is unavailable, the team should have a clear alternative communication process.

If a call is not attended, the concerned person can share the requirement through email or WhatsApp, or coordinate with an alternate colleague who can assist with the query. This will ensure that important matters do not remain pending simply because one particular person is unavailable.

Having a clearly defined backup or escalation system will also help maintain continuity of work while respecting employees’ personal time and avoiding unnecessary dependency on a single individual.
